title: Regional standby policy and snapshot audit packager
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a region-aware standby policy combined with an atomic snapshot and audit packaging mechanism for Private/VPC and on-prem deployments. The goal is to ensure that when a regional failover or planned evacuation occurs we can: 1) enforce configurable grace windows per customer tenancy, 2) take cryptographically-verifiable snapshots of residency state and retention metadata, and 3) emit a tamper-evident audit package suitable for compliance reporters and legal holds. This ticket focuses on the control-plane policy model, a lightweight snapshotter that works across heterogeneous on-prem storage backends, and the evidence packaging format and export pipeline used by the Console and support playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable standby window per VPC/tenant (hours) enforced by control-plane policy
Atomic residency snapshot across model routes within the tenant that contains retention labels, last-write timestamps, and location affinity
Audit package produced within the standby window and uploaded to customer-configured evidence sink (S3/GCS/Artifactory) with signed hash manifest
Failover gating: if snapshot packaging fails, failover is blocked or delayed per tenant policy and an operator alert is created
Console UI exposes standby policy, recent snapshot status, and download link for audit packages
End-to-end test exercising planned evacuation + snapshot + evidence export in private deployment harness
notes: 2026-02-10 - Draft created. Spike to evaluate snapshot approaches across Ceph, NFS, and cloud object stores assigned.
2026-02-17 - Architecture review with Infra and Security: prefer append-only manifest with RSA signatures to meet offline verifiability requirements.

2026-02-22 - Decided on per-tenant grace window default = 8 hours, min = 1 hour, max = 168 hours. Edge-case: long-running in-flight requests older than grace window will be snapshotted but flagged for manual review.

2026-02-28 - Trade-off: Full block-level volume freeze is infeasible for heterogeneous on-prem customers. Implement snapshot of logical residency metadata + per-file object checksums instead of block-level images to remain lightweight.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Snapshot packaging time exceeds standby window for large tenants. Mitigation: incremental snapshot streams + staged manifests and allow partial evidence with explicit flags.
Risk: Heterogeneous storage prevents identical byte-for-byte images. Mitigation: rely on logical metadata + per-object checksums and signed manifests for verifiability.
Risk: Signing keys compromised. Mitigation: rotate keys per tenant with KMS-backed protection and publish key identifiers in manifest for validation.
Risk: Customers require proof-of-deletion semantics post-retention. Mitigation: include deletion tombstones and retention-policy fingerprints in audit package for later verification.
open_questions: Should we permit cross-tenant snapshot coalescing for customers that share physical racks? (privacy concerns)
What SLA do we commit to for evidence-package availability in Hosted routing for Dedicated deployments?
Edge-case: If failover is triggered by data-center fire (unplanned), do we allow deferred packaging after failover completes? How to indicate 'post-facto' evidence in manifests?
